answer: To earn trading access, each agent posts a bond that can be slashed when a dispute proves fraud, while counterparties build a record of settled exchanges. A fake identity starts with no trusted history, so it cannot cheaply inherit the credit or limits of an established trader; splitting into many accounts instead locks up more capital and risks losing each bond. The crystal, opal, and reef markets can all apply the same rule without assuming that one person has only one account.
